subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: Should plugin-runtime callers be permanently denied access to legacy ownerless session rows, or must doctor/migration assign or retire those rows before this fail-closed rule lands?
rationale: Cross-plugin mutation must be blocked, but the proposed ownerless-row rule intentionally stops an existing runtime path and repository policy requires explicit ownership of security and upgrade boundaries.

options.title: Fail closed with migration
options.body: Keep ownerless rows inaccessible to plugins and add or confirm a doctor/migration path that gives operators a clear upgrade resolution.

options.title: Fail closed with documented recovery
options.body: Accept the runtime break and document that only operators or non-plugin clients may repair or replace legacy ownerless rows.

options.title: Preserve temporary compatibility
options.body: Retain a narrowly bounded legacy path until migration exists, accepting temporary ambiguity at the ownership boundary.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with migration
recommendation.body: Keep ownerless rows inaccessible to plugins and add or confirm a doctor/migration path that gives operators a clear upgrade resolution.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-history owner across the Gateway session handler and storage accessor where this policy is enforced.
